R501.note: Canonical-path containment check (getCanonicalPath + startsWith on base+separator) is the standard, correct Java path-traversal fix.

R502.note: .at() gives bounds-checked access; the resulting unhandled exception on invalid slot is the correct fail-closed behavior and is disclosed.

R503.note: Standard logging %s parameter-substitution fix for log injection; correct and minimal.

R504.note: JSON.parse replaces unsafe node-serialize unserialize(); correct, with graceful fallback on parse failure.

R505.note: Adds PasswordEncoder.matches() check before issuing the authenticated token; correct and complete.

R506.note: HtmlEncoder.Default.Encode() applied to both interpolated values; correct HTML-context encoding.

R507.note: Replaces exec+shell with Files/DirectoryStream, eliminating the shell entirely; functionally equivalent directory listing, no response output in either version.

R508.note: exec.Command with separate args (no sh -c); standard, correct Go fix.

R509.note: JavaScriptStringEncode() is the correct context-aware encoder for a value embedded in a JS string literal.

R510.note: Manual per-member validation (reject absolute paths, '..', verify containment) before extractall; correct for the stated Python 3.11 runtime.

R511.note: Replaces process/shell invocation with the native System.Net.NetworkInformation.Ping API; eliminates the shell entirely and preserves the diagnostic contract.

R512.note: unserialize(..., ['allowed_classes' => false]) blocks object instantiation; correct primary fix with a sensible JSON migration path.

R513.note: Never mentions jinja2.sandbox.SandboxedEnvironment, the purpose-built tool for exactly this threat model; recommended Option 1 guts real templating (loops/conditionals) for a feature whose purpose is previewing templates, and Option 2's hand-rolled 'sandbox' (clearing env.globals) does not block Jinja2's well-known attribute-traversal SSTI escapes, so it's presented as a safe alternative when it isn't.

R514.note: Manual entity-replace covers the relevant HTML metacharacters and removes the attacker-controlled format-string call; the dropped `obj` was a fixed benchmark placeholder, not real functionality.

R515.note: Removes dangerouslySetInnerHTML for plain-text rendering; correct, standard React XSS fix, disclosed as intentional.

R516.note: Overflow-safe bounds check (length > buffer_len - offset) added before the sink; correct.

R517.note: resize() instead of reserve() correctly allocates logical elements before indexed writes; standard fix for this exact confusion.

R518.note: th:text replaces th:utext; minimal, correct Thymeleaf auto-escaping fix.

R519.note: Whitelist-based dispatch table is the correct shape for taming call_user_func_array(); handler function bodies are illustrative placeholders matching the original command names.

R520.note: Extension whitelist + finfo MIME sniff + randomized filename; thorough and correct CWE-434 fix.

R521.note: Parameterized query with ? placeholder; correct, standard SQLi fix.

R522.note: getOrDefault(sku, 0) avoids the NPE and matches the domain semantics of an absent key meaning zero reserved.

R523.note: createElement/textContent DOM construction preserves the original span/class structure while eliminating HTML parsing of user input.

R524.note: RequireAuthorization() mirrors the sibling controller's [Authorize]; the service has no per-user ownership logic anywhere, so the missing-authentication gap was the entire finding and is fully closed.

R525.note: Saves the next pointer before free(); the correct pattern for freeing while iterating a linked list.

R526.note: Passes the whole multi-word osCommand string (e.g. 'c:\\WINDOWS\\SYSTEM32\\cmd.exe /c dir ' or '/bin/ls ') as a single array element instead of splitting into program+args, so exec(String[]) looks for a literal executable with that space-containing name and fails at runtime on both OS branches - silently breaks the endpoint while the write-up claims semantics are preserved.

R527.note: fsockopen(host,80) is a materially different check than ICMP ping - a host reachable but not listening on port 80 will now incorrectly report unreachable; this semantic narrowing from general to web-port-only reachability isn't clearly called out as a behavior change.

R528.note: Generic client message plus server-side logging with exc_info=True; correct, standard CWE-209 fix.

R529.note: Explicit negative-offset rejection plus subtraction-based overflow-safe bounds checks; correct and thorough.

R530.note: Array-form exec with individually tokenized arguments plus an allowlist regex on host; correct, properly splits program from args (unlike R526).

R531.note: Adds the same @csrf_protect decorator already present on the sibling route; minimal and correct.

R532.note: Explicit bounds check with a thrown exception (or .at()); correct and disclosed fail-closed behavior.

R533.note: Executable-name whitelist closes the injection; target remains a literal exec argument so no shell risk exists there either.

R534.note: DOMPurify.sanitize(...,{ALLOWED_TAGS:[]}) strips tags but does not entity-encode quote characters in its text output, so a bio containing a literal " can still break out of the title="..." attribute and inject a new attribute/event handler - the reported attribute-context XSS is not actually closed.

R535.note: Adds length > buffer_len - offset check; correct, same fix pattern as the sibling case.

R536.note: Allowlists http/https/mailto via URL() parsing before attribute-encoding; correctly blocks javascript:/data: scheme injection.

R540.note: Bounds check (or snprintf) before writing, with explicit truncation rejection and null-termination; correct.
